lessons.title: たしかさの だんかい
lessons.learn: Certainty is graded in four steps: かならず (certain), おそらく … でしょう (probable), ありえます (possible), ありえません (out of the question). The step chosen is a claim about the evidence, not about your mood.

grammar.title: Levels of certainty
grammar.pattern: かならず 〜ます · おそらく 〜でしょう · ありえます · ありえません
grammar.explain: かならず takes a plain affirmative, おそらく pairs with でしょう, and possibility is a verb: ありえます / ありえません. Writing たぶん with でしょう is weaker than おそらく and belongs in speech rather than in a report.

examples.en: It will certainly arrive tomorrow.

examples.en: The outlook will probably hold.

examples.t: その かのうせいも ありえます。
examples.en: That possibility is also open.

mistakes.why: おそらく takes でしょう and closes the sentence.

mistakes.wrong: ありえません と おもいます でしょう。
mistakes.right: ありえません。
mistakes.why: One certainty marker per sentence.

lessons.title: こんきょと すいろん
lessons.learn: Evidence and inference are kept in separate sentences: 〜から わかります (can be known from) and 〜に すぎません (no more than). と おもわれます marks what the field believes rather than what you do.

vocab.en: to be known, to be understood

grammar.title: Evidence and inference
grammar.pattern: 〜から わかります · 〜に すぎません · 〜と おもわれます · すいろんは べつです
grammar.explain: The evidence sentence names the material and から わかります; the inference takes と おもわれます or に すぎません. Mixing the two in one sentence is the failure the register exists to prevent.

lessons.title: はんいを きめる
lessons.learn: A claim is fenced before it is made: 〜に かぎり (as far as ~ is concerned), 〜を のぞいて (excluding), 〜の ばあい (in the case of). The fence is part of the claim, not a footnote.

grammar.title: Fencing a claim
grammar.pattern: 〜に かぎり · 〜を のぞいて · 〜の ばあいに かぎられます · はんいを かきます
grammar.explain: に かぎり is followed by the claim; を のぞいて removes a group; に かぎられます marks where the finding does apply. A claim with no fence claims the whole world.

examples.t: にじゅうだい を のぞいて、はんぶん です。
examples.en: Excluding people in their twenties, it is half.

examples.t: この ばあいに かぎられます。
examples.en: It applies to this case only.

mistakes.right: この データに かぎり、けいこうは つづいて います。
mistakes.why: The fence takes に かぎり and a full clause.

mistakes.wrong: にじゅうだい の のぞき、はんぶん です。
mistakes.right: にじゅうだい を のぞいて、はんぶん です。
mistakes.why: Exclusion takes を のぞいて.

lessons.title: です・ます と である
lessons.learn: The same page can be written in です・ます or in である, and the choice is announced by the whole document: である for reports and papers, です・ます for letters and notices, mixed only where a quotation begins.

grammar.title: Choosing a register
grammar.pattern: 〜である (report) · 〜です (notice) · レジスターを とういつします
grammar.explain: The register is chosen once and kept for the whole text; a switch mid-paragraph reads as an accident. The same sentence can be rephrased across registers without changing its content.

lessons.title: けいごの えらび
lessons.learn: Keigo is a choice about whose action it is: いらっしゃる (they come), うかがう (I go), いただく (I receive), さしあげる (I give). Choosing the wrong direction sounds worse than using no keigo at all.

vocab.t: ごらんに なります

grammar.title: Choosing keigo
grammar.pattern: いらっしゃる (their action, respectful) · うかがう (my action, humble) · いただく (my receiving) · さしあげる (my giving)
grammar.explain: Respectful forms raise the other person's action; humble forms lower my own. A humble verb on the other person's act is the error that marks a learner, so the test is always: whose action is it?

lessons.title: くだけた はなし
lessons.learn: Casual Japanese is a register, not a mistake: じゃ、だ、〜かな、〜だよ belong between people who know each other. The C1 skill is switching deliberately and never mixing the two inside one sentence.

grammar.title: Switching registers
grammar.pattern: じゃ、また · そうだよ · どう かな · 〜かも しれないな
grammar.explain: The casual register drops です・ます, contracts では to じゃ, and adds よ/ね/な for the listener. Switching is announced by the whole sentence — half-casual sounds worse than either register alone.

lessons.title: やさしい にほんごで つたえる
lessons.learn: Mediation starts by announcing the register: やさしい にほんごで おつたえします. Sentences shorten to one clause, kanji gain furigana, and every turn of phrase is marked with いいかえると.

grammar.title: Plain-language mediation
grammar.pattern: やさしい にほんごで おつたえします · ぶんせつを みじかく します · いいかえると、〜
grammar.explain: The rendering is announced, the clauses shorten to one idea each, and each rephrase is marked. Naming the change is what makes a plain rendering a service rather than a simplification of the reader.

lessons.title: やくしゃの ちゅうい
lessons.learn: The translator's note records what the rendering lost: やくしゃの ちゅうい として、〜が おちて います. おちます (to drop out) names the loss without complaining about it.

vocab.en: to drop out, to be lost

grammar.title: Translator's note
grammar.pattern: やくしゃの ちゅうい として、〜が おちて います · それは おぎなえません · ものたりなさ を かきます
grammar.explain: The note names the loss (〜が おちて います), states honestly that it cannot be made up (おぎなえません), and records the shortfall in ものたりなさ. Naming what a rendering loses is what keeps the original available to the reader.

culture.text: Mediation in Japanese runs through やさしい日本語, a public-service register with its own rules — one instruction per line, furigana, no double negatives — and through やくしゃの ちゅうい, the translator's note that records what a rendering loses. Both exist because Japanese carries politeness inside the sentence: a notice translated into plain language loses the keigo that made it polite, and the honest move is to write that loss down rather than pretend the two texts are the same.

reading.text: この おしらせは やさしい にほんごで おつたえします。いいかえると、あした の ごご までに もうしこんで ください、という いみです。ただし、やくしゃの ちゅうい として、ていねいさが おちて います。おぎなえませんから、ものたりなさ を かきます。この ことばは そのまま のこします。
reading.gloss: I will convey this notice in plain Japanese. In other words, it means: please apply by tomorrow afternoon. However, as a translator's note, the politeness is lost. Since it cannot be made up for, I will write the shortfall. This word I leave as it is.

task.title: Mediate one Japanese source for two different readers
task.instructions: Take any Japanese text of a few hundred characters — a notice, a report, a news item. Produce three outputs: (1) a plain-Japanese rendering announced with やさしい にほんごで おつたえします, shortened to one clause per line with furigana on the harder kanji; (2) the same content in である for a report; (3) a spoken version to a colleague with ようするに and one next step. Keep one key term from the original in each version, and finish with a やくしゃの ちゅうい that records what each rendering dropped. If any version sounds more certain than the source, lower it.
